part.overload.title: Overload
part.overload.summary: A piece with two duties cannot fulfil both: a check or a capture forces it to let go of one.
ex.ov.DWtI4: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.ov.DWtI4.hint: The knight on c3 defends the white queen on e4. Look for a check that only the knight can answer.
ex.ov.DWtI4.solution: 22...Rd1+! gives check, and only the knight on c3 can capture the rook. After 23.Nxd1, the queen on e4 is left undefended, and 23...Qxe4 captures it. With 22...Qd1+? the queen is lost to 23.Nxd1, and 22...Qxe4? only trades queens: after 23.Nxe4, Black is still a piece down.
ex.ov.Chiv8: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.ov.Chiv8.hint: The rook on c8 defends the black queen on c4. Look for a check that forces that rook off the c-file.
ex.ov.Chiv8.solution: 30.Rd8+! gives check, and the rook on c8 must capture. After 30...Rxd8, the queen on c4 is left undefended, and 31.Qxc4 captures it. With 30.Qxc4? the queens are only traded: after 30...Rxc4, White is still a piece down.
ex.ov.2YRoJ: Play as Black and find the best move. Your queen on f3 is attacked by the bishop and the queen.
ex.ov.2YRoJ.hint: The rook on c1 defends the white queen on c3. Look for a check on the king on e1.
ex.ov.2YRoJ.solution: 19...Rd1+! gives check, and only the rook on c1 can capture, because the queen on f3 watches d1. After 20.Rxd1, the queen on c3 is left undefended, and 20...Qxc3+ captures it with check. With 19...Qxc3+? the queens are only traded: after 20.Rxc3, Black is still a piece down.
ex.ov.pTV8S: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.ov.pTV8S.hint: The bishop on f6 defends the rook on g5. Look for a check that the bishop has to block.
ex.ov.pTV8S.solution: 25.Qh6+! gives check along the diagonal, and the bishop on f6 blocks on g7. After 25...Bg7, the rook on g5 is left undefended, and 26.Qxg5 captures it. With 25.Qxg5? the queen is lost: the bishop on f6 recaptures on g5.
ex.ov.uZFh9: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.ov.uZFh9.hint: The rook on d8 defends the black queen on d2. Which other square does that rook also guard?
ex.ov.uZFh9.solution: 25.Re8+! gives check, and only the rook on d8 can capture. After 25...Rxe8, the queen on d2 is left undefended, and 26.Qxd2 captures it. With 25.Qxd2? the queens are only traded: after 25...Rxd2, the position is equal.
ex.ov.7pUIL: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.ov.7pUIL.hint: The rook on e1 defends the white queen on e4. Which other piece does that rook also protect?
ex.ov.7pUIL.solution: 24...Rxf1+! captures the bishop with check. The king cannot recapture, because the bishop on h3 defends f1, and the rook on e1 must capture. After 25.Rxf1, the queen on e4 is left undefended, and 25...Qxe4 captures it. With 24...Qf2+? the advantage is gone: after 25.Kh1, White holds, and the game heads for a draw. With 24...Qxe4? the queens are traded, and White keeps the extra piece.
ex.ov.kGCK8: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.ov.kGCK8.hint: The rook on f2 defends the white queen on d2. Which move forces that rook off the second rank?
ex.ov.kGCK8.solution: 29...Nf3+! checks the king on g1 and attacks the queen on d2. If the king runs, the knight captures the queen. After 30.Rxf3, the rook leaves the second rank, and 30...Qxd2 captures the queen. With 29...Qxd2? the queens are only traded: after 30.Rxd2+, the position is equal.
ex.ov.eF6AG: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.ov.eF6AG.hint: The rook on e3 defends the white queen on e1. Which move forces that rook off the e-file?
ex.ov.eF6AG.solution: 42...Nf3+! checks the king on g1 and attacks the queen on e1. If the king runs, the knight captures the queen. After 43.Rxf3, the rook leaves the e-file, and 43...Qxe1+ captures the queen with check. With 42...Qg4+? the queen leaves the knight on d2 undefended, and after 43.Rg3 White is still a rook up. With 42...Qxe1+? the queens are traded, and Black is still a rook down.
part.removingDefender.title: Removing the defender
part.removingDefender.summary: If the target depends on a single defender, capture the defender first: the target is left unprotected.
ex.rd.3arLf: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.rd.3arLf.hint: The black bishop on f5 has only one defender. Which one is it?
ex.rd.3arLf.solution: 21.Qxg5! captures the queen, the only defender of the bishop on f5. After 21...hxg5, 22.Rxf5 captures the bishop, which was left undefended. With 21.Qc3?, you capture nothing, and the bishop on f5 stays defended. With 21.Rxf5?, the queen on g5 captures your queen on d2.
ex.rd.lkOry: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.rd.lkOry.hint: The white knight on b5 has only one defender. Which one is it?
ex.rd.lkOry.solution: 24...Rxd5! captures the rook that defended the knight on b5. After 25.exd5, 25...Qxb5 captures the knight, which was left undefended. With 24...Nf6?, 25.Nxc7 captures a pawn and attacks your queen. With 24...Qxb5?, the rook on d5 recaptures the queen.
ex.rd.GW4aE: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.rd.GW4aE.hint: The black bishop on d7 has only one defender. Which one is it?
ex.rd.GW4aE.solution: 22.Qxd5! captures the queen, the only defender of the bishop on d7. After 22...exd5, 23.Nxd7 captures the bishop, which was left undefended. With 22.Nxd7?, the queen on d5 captures your queen on e4.
ex.rd.9aToe: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.rd.9aToe.hint: The black rook on c4 has only one defender. Which one is it?
ex.rd.9aToe.solution: 29.Rxe6! gives up the rook for the bishop that defended the rook on c4. After 29...fxe6, 30.Qxc4 captures the rook, which was left undefended. With 29.Bxb7? or 29.Bd5?, the bishop on e6 stays in place and the rook on c4 remains defended. With 29.Qxc4?, the bishop on e6 recaptures the queen.
ex.rd.kYfHz: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.rd.kYfHz.hint: The white bishop on b5 has only one defender. Which one is it?
ex.rd.kYfHz.solution: 15...Nxc3! captures the knight that defended the bishop on b5. After 16.Rxc3, 16...Qxb5 captures the bishop, which was left undefended. With 15...a6?, 16.Bxc6 captures your knight on c6. With 15...Qxb5?, the knight on c3 recaptures the queen.
ex.rd.TKtNa: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.rd.TKtNa.hint: The white bishop on e5 has only one defender. Which one is it?
ex.rd.TKtNa.solution: 21...Bxf3! captures the knight that defended the bishop on e5. After 22.Qxf3, 22...Qxe5 captures the bishop, which was left undefended. With 21...Qb7?, the queen steps out of the attack, but 22.Bxb8 trades the bishop, and the game is equal. With 21...Qxe5?, the knight on f3 recaptures the queen.
ex.rd.XhY7A: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.rd.XhY7A.hint: The black bishop on e4 has only one defender. Which one is it?
ex.rd.XhY7A.solution: 19.Bxd6! captures the knight that defended the bishop on e4. After 19...Rxd6, 20.Bxe4 captures the bishop, which was left undefended. With 19.Bxe4?, the knight on d6 recaptures, and you win nothing.
ex.rd.UH275: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.rd.UH275.hint: Count the defenders of the rook on e8 and see what other piece each of them defends.
ex.rd.UH275.solution: 21.Rxd7! captures the bishop, one of the defenders of the rook on e8. The other is the rook on d8, which also defended the bishop: after 21...Rxd7, it leaves the eighth rank, and 22.Rxe8+ wins the rook. With 21.Rxe8+?, the bishop on d7 recaptures, and the game is equal. With 21.Bc4?, after 21...Rxe7 22.Rxe7 Be6, the bishop on e6 attacks your bishop, which cannot capture (23.Bxe6? Rd1#). After 23.Be2 Rb8 24.Bd3 Kf8, the black king attacks the rook on e7, and White gives up the rook for the bishop (25.Rxe6 fxe6).
part.trappedPiece.title: Trapped piece
part.trappedPiece.summary: A piece with no safe square is lost: attack it, or take away its last square.
ex.tp.KiNfu: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.tp.KiNfu.hint: The black bishop on d6 has few squares. Which move attacks it?
ex.tp.KiNfu.solution: 21.e5! attacks the bishop on d6, which has no safe square: c5 is covered by the bishop on e3, b4 by the pawn on a3 and a3 by the queen on c1. After 21...Bxe5 22.fxe5, White wins the bishop for a pawn. With 21.c4?, the bishop is not attacked, and the game is level.
ex.tp.u6em9: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.tp.u6em9.hint: The white bishop on d3 has few squares. Which move attacks it?
ex.tp.u6em9.solution: 15...e4! attacks the bishop on d3, hemmed in by its own pieces: the pawn on c4, the queen on c2 and the knight on e2 take away its squares, and the pawn on f5 defends e4. After 16.Bxe4 fxe4, Black wins the bishop for a pawn. With 15...f4?, the f5 square is freed, and the bishop on d3 gets out by capturing the pawn on g6.
ex.tp.dSPJV: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.tp.dSPJV.hint: The white queen on a7 has few squares. Which move attacks it?
ex.tp.dSPJV.solution: 16...Ra8! attacks the queen on a7, which has no safe square: on the a-file and on b8 the rook keeps attacking it, the bishop on b7 is defended by the queen on e7, and the knight on d5 defends b6. After 17.Qxa8+ Bxa8, Black wins the queen for a rook. With 16...c5?, the queen is not attacked and keeps its ways out, and White keeps the extra material.
ex.tp.m0gLC: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.tp.m0gLC.hint: The black rook on h8 has nowhere to go. Which piece can attack it?
ex.tp.m0gLC.solution: 13.Bd4! attacks the rook on h8 along the diagonal, and it has no square: the knight on g8 and the pawn on h7 hem it in. After 13...Nh6 14.Bxh8, White wins the rook. With 13.Bc4?, the knight on g8 goes to f6, and the rook on h8 gains the g8 square.
ex.tp.ZCV2v: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.tp.ZCV2v.hint: The black rook on d8 has few squares. Which of your bishops can take away the ones that are left?
ex.tp.ZCV2v.solution: 21.Bc7! attacks the rook on d8, which has no safe square: d7, d5 and c8 belong to the bishop on e6, and d6 and b8 to the bishop on c7. After 21...Rxe6 22.Bxd8, Black captures a bishop, but White wins the rook. With 21.Bxd4?, the bishop on c5 recaptures, and the bishop on e6 is still attacked by the rook on e8.
ex.tp.NDFeG: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.tp.NDFeG.hint: The black queen on c4 seems to have many squares. Count them one by one.
ex.tp.NDFeG.solution: 14.Re4! attacks the queen on c4, and all its squares are covered: the fourth rank and the e-file belong to the rook, d5, b5 and e2 to the knight on c3, and d3 and b3 to the pawns. After 14...Qxe4 15.Nxe4, White wins the queen for a rook. With 14.d3?, the queen escapes to d4 and attacks the rook on e3, which cannot leave the diagonal of your king, and the knight on g4 also attacks that rook.
ex.tp.hjRTt: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.tp.hjRTt.hint: The white rook on e6 has no safe square, but it has a defender.
ex.tp.hjRTt.solution: 19...Rxd4! The white rook on e6 has no safe square, but the knight on d4 defends it. The rook captures that defender, and after 20.Bxd4, 20...Qxe6 wins the rook, trapped and undefended. With 19...Qxe6?, the knight on d4 recaptures the queen.
ex.tp.M3L5f: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.tp.M3L5f.hint: The black bishop on h5 has no safe square. Who defends it?
ex.tp.M3L5f.solution: 12.Bxf6! The bishop on h5 has no safe square: g4 belongs to the queen on g3, f3 to the pawn on g2, e2 to the knight on f4 and d1 to the rook on f1. Only the knight on f6 defends it. After 12...Bxf6, 13.Nxh5 captures the bishop, which was left undefended. With 12.Nxh5?, the knight on f6 recaptures, and the pieces are simply traded.
